Confirmed from code and by a minimal repro. At ebd621d `OutboxRelay.rebuild()` (apps/infrx-api/infrx/state/outbox.py:48-49) is `dispatch_snapshot()` then `scheduler.rebuild(snapshot)` with nothing between or around them. In 0012 (apps/app/supabase/migrations/0012_dispatch_outbox.sql) `acknowledge_dispatch` stamps `acknowledged_at` unconditionally, `dispatch_pending` only returns rows `where o.acknowledged_at is null`, and `dispatch_snapshot` is one stable statement with no fence. So a job admitted after the snapshot read, indexed and acked by a pump before `scheduler.rebuild` lands, is in no index and is never redelivered; only another rebuild (index loss / process start) can bring it back, otherwise it sits `queued` until `queue_deadline_at`. Repro (memory scheduler + a stub store with exactly 0012's row semantics, scratchpad/strand.py): pump a; snap=snapshot; admit c; pump (indexed=1, acknowledged=1); q.rebuild(snap)=1; clock+31 s; pump reads 0; drain == {a}; c stranded with its row acked. Matches the reviewer's real-PostgreSQL drill on both images. Severity: it is a real data-path defect with a killable test, not style/docs/test-strength. It violates outbox.py's own unconditional claim ('no accepted job is ever missing from the index') and the DUR-OUTBOX oracle (04-verification.md: 'no missing accepted jobs', owner D/Q), and it is reachable in the wiring D2 itself prescribes (D2 evidence integration request 7: rebuild() at every scheduler start while pump() runs on a timer; any second process or an overlapping timer tick hits the window).
